acs.text: WHEN a room built with `createRoom` from `@sefaria-social/session` receives envelopes from its connections THE SYSTEM SHALL validate, limit and relay them as the reader's room does: a frame over 16 384 bytes is dropped, a 201st participant is refused, a connection's state messages beyond 20 per second are not relayed, and whatever a client puts in `from`, `seq`, `t` or `term` is replaced by the room's own values.
scenarios: The room enforces the reader's limits and stamps envelopes itself
A full room refuses the next participant

acs.text: WHEN a session client joins a room THE SYSTEM SHALL follow the spotlight holder (or the participant picked with `follow(id)`) by applying their stream through the reader state API with origin `follow`, and SHALL publish its own moment-scoped stream only while the room needs it and the `canPublish()` option allows it.
scenarios: A client follows the spotlight through the state API
A client publishes nothing while canPublish says no

acs.text: WHEN the WebSocket transport opens or reopens a connection THE SYSTEM SHALL ask its `protocols` callback for the subprotocols each time, so a fresh identity token travels in `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` and never in the URL.
scenarios: Each connection asks for fresh subprotocols

acs.text: WHEN the protocol fixtures (`packages/session/fixtures/protocol.v1.json`, results recorded with the reader's own room code) are replayed THE SYSTEM SHALL produce exactly the recorded result for every case, on the room side (`parseEnvelope`) and the client side (`parseRoomEnvelope`), and `LIMITS` and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` SHALL equal the recorded values; a change to either copy that alters a result makes the test fail and name the case.
scenarios: The reader's recorded protocol results still hold

acs.text: WHEN `npm run fixtures -w @sefaria-social/session -- --check <reader checkout>` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL recompute every expected result with the reader checkout's room code and fail naming each case whose result differs, and `packages/session/SOURCE.json` SHALL record the reader commit and the sha256 of every file copied from it.
scenarios: A drift check against a reader checkout names the differing case
